A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete, readable main text and Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to the arXiv stamp and acknowledgments.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of three CRL methods on real and simulated light-tunnel data in Section 3, supervised recovery experiments in Appendix B, and simulator validation in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 3 and Appendices B–C unchanged.

M1.justification: The light-tunnel setup, deterministic simulator, model adaptations, and training procedures in Sections 2–3 and Appendices A–C are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same real image and sensor datasets, interventional, multiview and temporal tasks, synthetic counterparts, and simulator-training datasets.

E2.justification: The evaluated methods remain Contrastive CRL (Buchholz et al., 2023), multiview CRL (Yao et al., 2024c), and CITRIS (Lippe et al., 2022). The supervised check in Appendix B is also retained.

E3.justification: Reported sample counts, splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, and training budgets are identical in Section 3 and Appendix A.

E4.justification: The synthetic ablations, CITRIS configuration trials in Appendix A.3.2, supervised recovery check in Appendix B, and simulator checks in Appendix C are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same five random initializations and uncertainty summaries, including means and standard deviations in Figures 3, 6, and 9.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match across the main text and appendices. For example, Figure 3 retains CCRL MCC values of 0.285 ± 0.054 on real data and 0.891 ± 0.005 on synthetic data.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, causal-process specifications, metric definitions, and simulator derivations in the main text and Appendices A and C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The contribution remains a real-world CRL sanity check, with the same claims about method failures, reproducibility difficulties, and mixing-function assumptions.

C2.justification: The explanations of method failures and limitations on evaluating latent causal assumptions and generalizing benchmark success remain identical in Sections 2–4.

D1.justification: v2 newly acknowledges use of DKRZ resources allocated by its Scientific Steering Committee under project ID 1083. This adds limited resource provenance; Appendix A already specifies A100 GPUs and approximately 100 GPU hours, and all implementation and access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to existing CRL methods and benchmarks are identical. The added DKRZ acknowledgment introduces no research citation or positioning change.

P1.justification: v2 adds one resource-acknowledgment sentence and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose, terminology, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded acknowledgment shifts the Impact Statement downward on page 9. Figures, tables, captions, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added DKRZ credit modestly improves resource attribution, while the scientific evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility instructions remain unchanged. Appendix A already supplied GPU and compute-time details, so the acknowledgment and small presentation edits produce no meaningful overall quality difference.
